title: 5. The Fourth Method of Correlative Thinking — Convergence (融合)
content:
### 5.1. The Definition of Convergent Thinking

In Chapter 4, we showed that "empathy" through Logos is not mere emotional sympathy but a powerful, distinctively human measure that discerns the social norms and the good and evil of an age. Having sought the root (mimesis), formed relationships (mythos), and erected order (Logos), humanity now stands before the final stage of evolution. Beyond analyzing and discerning, a great integration is required that completely blends East and West, machine (AI) and the whole of human civilization into one at a cosmic level, weaving a new framework. This is why the thinking of Chapter 5 [Part I's fourth method], convergence (融合)—the completion of the four modes of correlative thinking—appears.

Convergence is not recklessly mixing this and that. It is the work of bringing out the strengths of different elements to make a new order that did not exist before. It is easy to understand if we recall *bibimbap*. The mixing of the ingredients does not make each flavor disappear; rather, the overall flavor becomes richer.

It is the same with scholarship. Philosophy alone cannot solve all technological problems, and engineering alone cannot solve all ethical problems. History and religion, economy and science, and art must meet for the complex problems of the AI era to be handled properly.

By analogy with a middle-school student's study, convergence is using together the reading ability of Korean, the institutional understanding of social studies, and the analytic ability of science to solve a single problem. For the problems of real life always overlap several subjects.

The fourth stage, "convergence (融合)," signifies creatively synthesizing diverse elements—ideas, cultures, methodologies, even the capacities of human and machine—to make something new and more powerful. It embodies the principle of "consilience." One of the core themes is to aim at a "hybrid thinker" by integrating the holistic wisdom of the East (correlative thinking) with the analytic rationality of the West. "Liminal spaces"—transitional, in-between states in which ordinary rules are suspended—are fertile soil for "creativity, flexibility, and connection" and for the emergence of new synthesis. AI itself is leading society into such a liminal stage. The Korean popular-culture phenomenon "Hallyu (the Korean Wave)" is presented as an example of a successful cultural "convergence" that mixed local and foreign elements to create something new and globally resonant. Korea's "*bibim* (mixing)" culture is sometimes likened to a "yin-yang convergence" that offers ethical and creative insight.

As concrete methodologies of convergence, "structurology" seeks to integrate heterogeneous fields of mathematics into a coherent system and to understand phenomena through their fundamental connective structure (Kim Dong-ryeol, 2010); "TRIZ" is a systematic problem-solving methodology that synthesizes principles from diverse fields to create innovative solutions (Kim Ho-jong et al., 2011); and "Human Design" is presented as a system that integrates ancient wisdom (the *Book of Changes*, Kabbalah, the chakras) with modern science (genetics, physics) to explain the individual's uniqueness (Krakower et al., 2018). The ultimate goal is a "new human–AI co-evolution," the convergence of human and machine.

"Convergence" is, beyond merely mixing existing elements, the process of creating emergent properties and new solutions that transcend the sum of the parts. This is especially important in the AI era, which faces unprecedented challenges. The discussion of liminal spaces suggests that truly new forms emerge in such "in-between" spaces. Methodologies such as TRIZ and Human Design are not mere collections of ideas but frameworks for generating new insight through synthesis. This means that human creativity in the AI era will increasingly lie in "creative connectivity"—that is, in fusing diverse domains of knowledge, including knowledge AI can generate, into a new and valuable whole.

The success of cultural convergence such as Hallyu provides a model by which society can navigate globalization and technological change—not by resisting outside influence or losing its identity, but by creatively integrating it. This is "convergence" as a civilizational strategy. The call for "convergence" implies the need to break down traditional disciplinary barriers in education and research and to cultivate a more interdisciplinary and transdisciplinary approach so that the human can prepare for a complex future. If a "hybrid thinker" is needed, then the educational system must change to cultivate one. The following table summarizes the diverse methodologies that embody the principle of "convergence" in the AI era.

**Table 5: Methodologies of "Convergence (融合)" in the AI Era**

| Methodology | Core principle | Application in the AI era |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Correlative thinking | Holistic, relational, contextual understanding | Ethical governance of AI, design of human–AI interaction, sustainable management of complex socio-technical systems |
| Exploration of liminality | Creativity, flexibility, and the emergence of new synthesis in transitional spaces | Managing the social and occupational transitions caused by AI adoption, designing new norms and institutions, experimenting with human–AI collaboration models |
| Structurology | Exploring the regularity of connection among separated elements, integrating diverse fields into a coherent logical system, valuing the form of information transmission | Understanding the inner workings of complex AI systems, optimizing data structures and information flow, improving the stability and predictability of AI-based systems |
| TRIZ | Systematic problem-solving and innovation through resolving contradictions, applying inventive principles, and pursuing the Ideal Final Result (IFR) | Overcoming the limits of AI algorithms, pioneering new fields of AI application, solving the unexpected problems of AI technology, developing innovative solutions through human–AI collaboration |
| Human Design | Understanding the individual's unique energy flow, potential, and decision-making style through the integration of ancient wisdom and modern science | Redefining the individual's strengths and roles in the AI era, customized education and career development, optimizing complementarity in forming human–AI teams, promoting individual well-being |
| "*Bibim*" culture | Creating new value and identity through the harmonious mixing of diverse elements (local/foreign, traditional/modern) | Creatively combining global AI technology with local culture, contextualizing AI ethics and policy culturally, developing AI solutions through the collaboration of teams with diverse backgrounds |

### 5.2. The Fourth Mode of Thought: ∀X, Theos

We have grasped the infinite power of convergence, which breaks down boundaries and forges entirely new cosmic value. If multidimensionality, circulation, and empathy each sought the root of life, formed relationships, and erected order, now it is the turn of the great furnace to appear that melts all this thought into one and sublimates it into a new galaxy. That is precisely Theos, the "fourth mode of thought" that embraces all things—for which this age has been desperately waiting.

The Abrahamic religions (Christianity, Catholicism, Islam), which say "X is everything," pursue the eternal life of the soul (靈魂永生) through a covenantal circulation, grounded in the Ten Commandments, between God and the human community. Because the Ten Commandments and the Lord's Prayer contain all of heaven-earth-human (corresponding to Confucianism-Buddhism-Daoism), "X is everything." The logic of "X is everything," since it pursues community over the individual and spirit over matter, comes to pursue eternal life through the soul.

This expression does not mean that all boundaries completely disappear, but that each being is connected within a larger whole. A single person is part of a family, part of a school community, and also part of society and history. The sense that the small one is not severed from the great whole is contained here.

Simply put, a single piece of trash I throw away is connected to environmental problems, and a single comment I post is connected to someone's day. My choice does not end with me alone. So "X is everything" is also a sentence of immense responsibility.

In the AI era, this thinking matters more. For one company's algorithm, one nation's technology policy, and one individual's habit of use affect the trust and safety of the whole world.

As the fourth mode of thought, "X is everything (∀X)" can be linked to a pantheistic perspective, containing the insight that all beings are fundamentally connected as one and that individual things are diverse manifestations of the whole. This suggests the possibility that, beyond the dichotomous boundaries between part and whole, subject and object, human and nature, and further between human and machine, everything can mutually interpenetrate and converge. In the AI era, such thinking can open a new ontological horizon beyond anthropocentrism.

#### 5.2.1. The Dismantling of the Credentialist Society and the Shift of Power

A representative field among these new horizons is the credentialist society. Existing fields disappear and new ones appear. The age in which life was decided by college entrance exams is being shaken ever more by AI. More than the fact of having graduated from a particular elite university, what one can actually do is becoming more important. AI has democratized access to information. Knowledge once obtainable only through a good professor or expensive textbooks is now open to anyone through online lectures and AI tools. This is becoming a force that accelerates the cracking of the credential monopoly.

But this change does not automatically make an equal society. For the very ability to use AI well can become a new privilege. Classes that find it hard to access computers and the internet, people who cannot afford to learn AI tools, and non-English speakers who cannot fully use English-based AI because of the digital language gap—these risk becoming the new digitally alienated class. Seen through the eyes of *hwajaeng*, even after the dismantling of the credentialist society, power does not disappear; it merely changes form and shifts. What matters is consciously designing that new power structure to be fairer and more open.

The advance of AI technology fundamentally changes the modes of production, distribution, and access to knowledge, and is dismantling the foundation of the traditional credentialist society. The power once maintained through the monopoly of knowledge and information is losing its force as it becomes universally accessible through AI. Seen from the perspective of "X is everything," knowledge and wisdom are not confined to a particular class or institution but exist everywhere in diverse forms, and AI can play the role of connecting and amplifying this dispersed wisdom. Therefore power shifts not to past credentials or status, but to the ability to fuse diverse knowledge, create new value, and present solutions to complex problems.

#### 5.2.2. The Convergence of East and West and of Human and Machine

The true wisdom of the AI era can be manifested when the East's mimetic (complementary, imitative) thinking and mythic (narrative, symbolic) thinking, and the West's logocentric (logical, analytic) thinking, are fused with the human's experiential wisdom and the machine's data-based intelligence. The perspective of "X is everything" shows that these diverse systems of thought and forms of wisdom are not mutually exclusive but can be integrated complementarily. The following table presents cases and features of East–West resonance applicable in the AI era.

**Table 6: Methodologies of "East–West Resonance" in the AI Era**

| Eastern resonance | Western resonance |
| --- | --- |
| Yin-yang and five phases, dependent arising, the Mean (中庸) | Systems theory, complexity science, ecology |
| The Limitless (無極), emptiness (虛), the Middle Way (中道) | Studies of rites of passage, the early stages of "disruptive innovation" in innovation theory |
| Pattern recognition of the *Hetu-Luoshu* (河圖洛書), the interactive structure of the five phases | Topology, network theory, systems architecture |
| The strategic thinking of Sunzi's *Art of War* (overcoming contradiction), the application of the principles of change in the *Book of Changes* (易) | Invention studies, engineering design methodology, Creative Problem Solving (CPS) |
| The *I Ching*, the chakra system, elements of the study of fate | Genetics, quantum physics, biochemical individuality |
| The harmony of yin-yang, harmony-without-uniformity (和而不同) | Cultural fusion, hybrid innovation |

The human can use AI's analytic capacity to reinterpret Eastern wisdom in a modern way, and at the same time, through Eastern insight, lead the ethical and humane development of AI technology. Such convergent wisdom will become the core driving force for solving the complex problems of the AI era and creating a new civilization.

### 5.3. A New Image of the Human: *Gwanwang* and *Dosol*

*Gwanwang* (冠旺) is the stage that comes after *yokdae* among the Twelve Stages of the study of fate, signifying the period of having reached a peak in which one wears a cap (*gwan*) and one's energy is flourishing (*wang*). In this work, in accord with that meaning, it signifies the mature adult and the autonomous conductor who embraces and "commands" all the preceding stages—*po-tae* (possibility), *yangsaeng* (embodiment), and *yokdae* (ethical discernment).

*Gwanwang* (冠旺) is the symbol of a figure who harmonizes complex situations with outstanding wisdom and judgment. This is not merely someone with much knowledge or excellent skill, but someone with the wisdom to recognize the abilities of different people and let each shine in their own place. The core human role needed in the AI era is precisely this image of *gwanwang*. AI is a powerful instrument, but an instrument does not make music by itself. A human like *gwanwang* must decide in which piece, at what intensity, and within what harmony to play the instrument that is AI.

Translated into an analogy familiar to a middle-school student, *gwanwang* is like an excellent team leader or class president. It is the person who does not pretend to do everything well, but recognizes what each team member does best, divides roles, and fairly harmonizes conflicts when they arise. In the AI era, such a person is also the one who uses AI best. The ability to judge what work to entrust to AI, what work the human must do, and how to review AI's results is the modern role of *gwanwang*.

Into what kind of being must the human be reborn in the AI era? The analogy of "*gwanwang* (冠旺)" and "*dosol* (兜率)" offers one answer to this question.

#### 5.3.1. The Human as *Gwanwang* (冠旺)

An AI agent is an AI program that autonomously performs a particular task. In the near future will come an age in which dozens of AI agents work simultaneously for the individual, for the corporation, for the government. Information-gathering agents, schedule-management agents, customer-response agents, decision-support agents—all operate at once. To use this complex legion of agents properly requires a human harmonizing ability like that of *gwanwang*. Which agent to entrust with which task, how to harmonize the agents when they conflict with one another, how to verify the agents' results—all these judgments are the human's portion.

For *gwanwang*'s leadership to function effectively, two abilities are needed. The first is knowing accurately the capacities and limits of AI. If one cannot distinguish what the agents do well from what they do poorly, one entrusts the wrong work to the wrong agent. The second is the attitude in which the human takes final responsibility for the results AI produces. However good a result an agent produces, the responsibility for that result's effect on people falls, in the end, on people. This sense of responsibility is the core that protects the human as *gwanwang* in the AI era.

*Gwanwang* symbolizes the image of a leader who harmonizes and leads complex situations with outstanding wisdom and insight. The human of the AI era, like the conductor of an orchestra, must perform the role of a "*gwanwang*" who harmoniously coordinates countless AI agents and automated systems and leads them toward a common goal. This requires, beyond merely controlling AI, the highly advanced wisdom and judgment to bring out AI's potential to the fullest while preventing ethical problems and realizing human-centered values.

#### 5.3.2. The Realization of *Dosolcheon* (兜率天)

*Dosol* (兜率) is the transliteration of *Dosolcheon* (Tuṣita), the ideal realm in the Buddhist cosmology where Maitreya, the future Buddha, dwells. In this book, beyond its original spatial meaning, a homophonic and ideational context is deliberately assigned: the binding of countless AI agents into one to lead and "command (統率)" them all. Because this accords with the image of *gwanwang*, it is used in connection as one of the stages of human growth.

*Dosolcheon* is, in Buddhism, the ideal world where Maitreya dwells, signifying a Pure Land full of wisdom and compassion. In the AI era, "*Dosolcheon*" can be a metaphor for an ideal state in which human will and creativity can be infinitely expanded and realized through the AI network. The human, taking AI as a tool and partner for realizing their own will, can carry out creative activity beyond individual limits and, further, be reborn as an "expanded human" who contributes to the welfare and development of society as a whole. This is the image of a future society that can be made through the harmonious coexistence of technology and the human.

### 5.4. The Final Stage of Completion: Convergence

We can picture a truly mature image of the human, advancing under the command of *gwanwang* (the commander) toward the grand ideal of *Dosolcheon*. Humanity, having passed narratively through *po-tae*, *yangsaeng*, and *yokdae*, finally comes to wield cosmic command at ease. Now the moment of "convergence"—the final knot of that majestic and holy great journey of thought, and the ultimate goal point that hyperconnected civilization must reach—arrives before us.

Seeing with multidimensionality, reading with circulation, connecting with empathy, and finally creating something new through convergence. When these four stages are completed, the human becomes not a mere user of AI but a designer of the civilization of the AI era. The word "completer" may sound grandiose, but the essence is simple. It means that the human is not one who merely accepts the world AI has made, but a being who chooses and takes responsibility for what kind of world to make.

The most important thing the human, as completer, must do in the hyperconnected society is to ask "good questions." AI quickly produces answers to questions, but which questions are important must be decided by the human. Just as this entire work began from a single great question—"how can humanity survive together in the AI era?"—future generations too must pose large, important questions suited to their own age. The wisdom of correlative thinking and *hwajaeng* is the most human training for cultivating the power of that question.

Convergence, the final stage of correlative thinking, means that the human, on the basis of the insight and ability gained through multidimensionality, circulation, and empathy, performs the role of an autonomous "completer" in the hyperconnected AI society. This is, beyond merely adapting to technology, the process of actively using technology in accord with human value and purpose and of creating a new civilizational ecosystem in which human and AI mutually develop. Through convergent thinking, the human will build, beyond division and conflict, an order of mutual flourishing and harmony, and will become the creative protagonist who leads the infinite possibilities of the AI era to the prosperity of all humanity.
